analysis: Both units are CHANGELOG.md documentation-only head-text excerpts (lines 389-~700). No executable code, config, or mode changes are present, so no code-level security regression can be derived from them. The prose describes security-relevant behavior already modeled in the canonical threat model: App Attest serving authorization (TB-011, T-052..T-058), durable build qualification and revocation (A-017, T-054), legacy MDM/APNs coexistence (TB-009, T-036), encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041; the 30-minute TTL and available-disk/2 budget wording matches the model), account-scoped cache salt, and the privacy descriptions that remove unsupported memory-wiping and forward-secrecy claims (consistent with T-003/T-011). The changelog statements state that serving/removal stay disabled by default and that fresh proof, qualified build, nonrevoked key and current connection checks are still required, so no assumption is invalidated by the text. The actual implementing code (coordinator appattest/service, provider changes, drain barrier, first-content SLA account selection via EIGENINFERENCE_FIRST_CONTENT_SLA_ACCOUNTS, Responses instruction lowering, token-promotion ledger) is not in these units, so the claims are unverified; later passes should review those source files if supplied. A drain-barrier coordinator/provider deployment-ordering note (0.9.8) is an operational concern only. Coverage limit: only the changelog was examined.
